clue.text: Fall within the bounds of boffins' intelligence

indicators.note: within says the synonym for fall sits inside the letters taken from boffins'
the bounds of a word are its first and last letters, here of boffins'

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky, so fall can mean rain

explanation.surface: Something drops into the reach of the clever scientists' brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is an everyday informal word for cleverness or mental ability.

clue.text: Ben is without a pulse

indicators.note: is without here means is outside, so the name Ben wraps around the next piece

explanation.surface: A man named Ben is found to have no heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is an edible seed such as a lentil or bean, so a bean is an example.

clue.text: Mark, perhaps, made on a spoon

definitions.meaning: Mark the evangelist, loosely counted among Christ's followers sent out to preach
... spoons have a figure of one of the twelve disciples moulded on the handle

explanation.surface: Asking whether Mark was crafted into a piece of cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a disciple sent to preach, and apostle spoons carry such figures on the handle.

clue.text: No change to starlet right away — rated more highly than some

indicators.note: change to says the letters of the following words are to be rearranged
away says the abbreviation for right is removed from starlet

explanation.surface: Telling a young actress to change nothing and leave at once, as she outranks others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' leaves STALET, which 'change to' rearranges; the opening word of the clue stays unscrambled at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is 'not least' means it ranks above some others in importance.

clue.text: Some beds could be raised to give relief

indicators.note: could be says the letters of some beds may be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A few beds might be lifted up to offer comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: An embossed design is raised from the surface, as in relief carving.

clue.text: Trousers I'm to drop around about one for skin cream

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the piece for one
trousers dropped around the ankles are in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man lets his trousers fall while applying lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a man dropping his trousers; 'drop around' is the anagram signal, and 'about' is a separate container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moisturiser is a cream applied to keep skin from drying out.

clue.text: Unacceptable company from the beginning

parts.note: out means unacceptable or not allowed, as in 'that idea is out'
a set is a group of people who keep company together

explanation.surface: A bad crowd has been present right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the start of something, as in 'from the outset'.

clue.text: Waves breaking over the champion could be the finish

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: surf is the foam of waves breaking on the shore
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: Crashing waves overwhelm the title-holder and might end his run.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface finish is the outer coating or texture given to an object.

clue.text: After ten years, North Carolina has the first bit of evidence of corruption

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the period of ten years

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NC is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Carolina

indicators.note: the first bit of evidence is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Ten years on, a US state finally has some proof of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral decline or decay, a kind of corruption.

clue.text: Fosters? Make a choice without the commercials

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the commercials wrap around the choice

parts.note: ads are commercials or advertisements
to opt is to make a choice

explanation.surface: A lager drinker chooses a brand with no advertising to sway them.
explanation.walkthrough: Fosters suggests the Australian lager, but it is the verb: to foster or take in a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child is to take it into one's family, much as one fosters it.

clue.text: 22 is, or could be, momentous

indicators.note: could be says the letters before it may be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: the number points to the answer of clue 22, a word for a yen or longing

explanation.surface: A clue number, plus is or, might be rearranged into something momentous.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' stands for the answer to 22-down; 'could be' rearranges it with IS and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means significant enough to be remembered in history, i.e. momentous.

clue.text: The best a bandit could produce — it tops the lot!

indicators.note: could produce says the letters of the preceding words might yield a new phrase

explanation.surface: A one-armed bandit's top payout is the best thing there is.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something surpasses everything else, an informal superlative.

clue.text: Some jumpers in the soup?

parts.note: jumpers are pullovers with high rolled collars, but read cryptically they are the necks of reptiles that end up in a soup

explanation.surface: Asking whether certain sweaters have fallen into a bowl of broth.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of high-collared sweater shares its name with a sea reptile's neck, and turtle soup is a classic dish.

clue.text: Managers of funds sure to be involved in unexpected arrest

indicators.note: to be involved in says sure goes inside the other letters
unexpected says the letters of arrest come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Fund managers are certain to be caught up in a surprise arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' turns the arrest letters into TREARS, which is split open after TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasurers are officers who look after an organisation's money.

clue.text: Bail out — air outside initially stresses vertebra's extremities

indicators.note: outside says the word for air goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: an air is a tune, and a tone is a musical sound

indicators.note: out says the letters of bail are scattered
initially means take the opening letter of stresses

explanation.surface: Getting released from custody while the atmosphere puts strain on one's backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail out' reads as being released or bailing water; 'out' jumbles it to AILB, and 'air' is a musical tone, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones at the base of the spine, collectively the coccyx, sit at the backbone's lower end.

clue.text: Low average?

definitions.meaning: low in the sense of base, stingy or contemptible
the arithmetic average of a set of numbers

explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something low or petty, and in maths the mean is the average.

clue.text: A top craftsman once supreme in the house?

definitions.meaning: a tradesman who works on top of buildings, laying straw roofs
a former Prime Minister who dominated the House of Commons in the 1980s

explanation.definitionFit: A roofer who uses straw or reed is so named, as was Margaret, the UK Prime Minister 1979 to 1990.

clue.text: A small part of the foot?

definitions.text: A small part of the foot?

parts.words: A small part of the foot?
parts.note: reads like a toe or heel, but the foot is the unit of length, with twelve smaller units

explanation.definitionFit: This imperial unit is a twelfth of a foot as a measure of length.

clue.text: Keyboard Claire's arranged to see about five

indicators.note: about says the jumbled name goes round the numeral
arranged says the letters of the name are put in a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, so the name alone is the fodder
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Claire has set up a piano to accompany five singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges CLAIRE into CLAIER, and 'about' wraps it round V.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is an early keyboard instrument, or the keyboard itself.

clue.text: It's clearly a good place for growing tomatoes

definitions.text: It's clearly a good place for growing tomatoes

parts.words: It's clearly a good place for growing tomatoes
parts.note: clearly hints at a transparent building, since it is made of panes that let light in for plants

explanation.definitionFit: A glass-walled building where plants such as tomatoes are raised in warmth.

clue.text: More perfect?

parts.note: describes something idealised beyond the real, like Thomas More's imaginary perfect island

explanation.definitionFit: Utopian means idealistically perfect, from the island in Sir Thomas More's book.

clue.text: Creature running wild in Guiana

indicators.note: running wild says the letters of Guiana are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal roams free in the South American region.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical lizard, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Unconventional people into social philosophy and whale reproduction

parts.note: to whale is to thrash or beat someone
generation is the act of producing offspring

explanation.surface: Eccentric thinkers interested in society and how whales breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whale' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation were 1950s American writers who rejected conventional society.

clue.text: Leaders of International Trade Corporation holding yen

indicators.note: leaders of means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Heads of a global trading company have a stake in Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like a container indicator, but it supplies its own first letter; 'yen' is a craving, not the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a longing or craving, as is an urge one wants to scratch.

clue.text: The pest is in touch

indicators.note: in says is sits inside the word for touch

parts.note: a touch is a subtle shade or hint, as is a nuance

explanation.surface: The annoying creature is within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is someone or something annoying, which is what a nuisance means.

clue.text: Move right in — a penance at one time

indicators.note: in says the letter for right goes inside the word for move

parts.note: to shift is to move

explanation.surface: Stepping to the right to do penance, as was once the custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift was the old term for confession and penance imposed by a priest.

clue.text: Seaweed and rags recycled, as in the manner indicated

indicators.note: recycled says rags is reprocessed into a new order

parts.note: so means thus, in the way shown

explanation.surface: Seaweed and old cloth are reused as shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a floating brown seaweed that gives the Sargasso Sea its name.

clue.text: Painful separation of church architect and church?

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches

explanation.surface: A designer of churches parting painfully from his church.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden painful parting, as in leaving home being a wrench.
